season_garden_12_001.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_001.text: The twelfth visit began with a clear patch of sky and wet earth that did not belong to a new storm. Staff had watered the appropriate beds before the helpers arrived. Yue smelled the dampness at the open hall door and almost mistook it for the weather returning. Qiu pointed to the dry roof edge, then waited while Yue looked again. The garden had become familiar enough to invite guesses. Familiarity could help them notice a change, but it could also make the first explanation arrive too quickly.

season_garden_12_002.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_002.text: Su set the day's light assignments beside the usual supported table. The responsible gardener had offered a fresh inspection of the selected planting, with maintenance decisions still theirs. The family gathering remained planned after the fourteenth session, subject to current permission and conditions. Today's inspection would not be turned into an update for the grandmother who had died. Yue held the empty space where she once imagined the little message going. She could still notice living things without pretending their growth supplied an answer to her death.

season_garden_12_003.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_12_003.text: “I used to want the next improvement to make the last disappointment look necessary,” Qiu said as they prepared the small light record board. “If something good followed, then I could call the earlier pain useful.” Yue said she had tried that with a difficult exercise once and disliked how much it excused. Qiu looked toward the garden. “The plant doesn't owe us that story.” They checked the board's ordinary tie and left the sentence there, between them, without trying to make it part of the public account.

season_garden_12_004.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_004.text: The actual selected planting determined what they could inspect today. Annual seedlings and a young plum asked different questions of the gardener and gave different things to see. The helpers would make the corresponding light observations only under the gardener's direction, then return to the shared repair work. Yue's earlier preference still mattered through the living thing or bed actually established. It did not give either woman permission to revise the season into an easier history now that the person who had asked for yellow flowers was gone.

season_garden_12_005.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_005.text: After the garden inspection, a maintenance worker showed them the old tree's still restricted ground from the permitted side of the marker. The crown had been removed earlier by qualified workers. Root and surface conditions needed their own current review; the helpers were not to infer safety from a cleaner view. Qiu could see a tempting patch that looked ready for ordinary use. The worker explained a shallow change hidden under the surface. Yue watched Qiu accept that unseen work did not become imaginary merely because her gauge could not measure it.

season_garden_12_006.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_006.text: The bench owner came out with her empty onion basket and stood at the permitted edge. Her son wanted the old tree's story to end with a replacement large enough to restore the former view. She said no tree could be bought already carrying forty years of their household's afternoon shade. She was not opposing new planting. She was refusing to have the missing years treated as a defect in the new tree. Yue heard a harder kind of patience than waiting for a seed to show itself.

season_garden_12_007.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_12_007.text: “I thought replacement was the hopeful part,” Yue said. The owner answered that replacement could be useful and still fail to replace a particular person, branch or summer. She set the basket on the safe side and named where her husband had usually put his feet. Qiu looked at the present space and did not try to put an outline of his body there. The owner pointed to the open sky. She had begun noticing evening birds she could not see from the old shaded seat. She liked them without calling the loss fortunate.

season_garden_12_008.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_008.text: A worker asked whether the basket might move so the clear route stayed clear. The owner shifted it without offense and continued telling the story from a different angle. Yue noticed that an ordinary practical interruption had not destroyed the memory. Nobody needed to freeze the garden to show respect. Qiu offered the owner her supported drawing surface only if she wanted to indicate a place. She declined, laughing that the sky could not be made flatter by drawing it. The basket went back indoors with its owner when she finished speaking.

season_garden_12_009.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_009.text: The helpers' next task was a shallow removable drawer cover from existing stock, already assigned for ordinary light handling. It protected paper from casual splashes at the work table; it did not preserve a patient's information in an unattended public place. Yue checked the folded edge with her arm supported. Qiu was inclined to make the fit so close that opening it became awkward. They tried it three times using the hand movements an actual hall worker would make. On the third attempt, Qiu admitted that a looser edge gave the person a better purchase.

season_garden_12_010.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_12_010.text: “A perfect fit can be an inconvenient thing,” Qiu said. Yue asked whether she intended to apply that discovery to every previous argument between them. Qiu said she would need a much larger drawer. Both laughed, and the owner called from the doorway that larger drawers mostly held more forgotten rubbish. Yue had a sudden image of every carefully won measurement stored among lost buttons. Qiu looked offended on behalf of the gauge, then made the ordinary edge easier to lift. The joke had found its way into the useful adjustment.

season_garden_12_011.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_011.text: A kitchen worker wanted to keep one old paper bag inside the drawer because it still held a sound cord. Another wanted the bag discarded because it resembled a note someone should read. The helpers asked what actually needed storing. The cord could go into the ordinary labeled compartment; the worn bag had no task left. Yue checked whether anyone owned it before removing it from use. The decision was disappointingly small. She had wanted a sweeping act of tidiness, and instead had to ask one person about one bag.

season_garden_12_012.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_012.text: Qiu's private practice notes lay beside her belongings, separate from the garden's shared arrangement. Yue saw a little line of numbers and asked what they measured. Qiu said they recorded how quickly she could complete a controlled familiar exercise without increasing its strain. It was her own practice, outside the paid garden task and under her actual limits. She would not demonstrate it to the visitors who sometimes mistook her work clothes for an invitation. Yue asked whether the numbers satisfied her. Qiu said some days they did and some days they became another hungry mouth.

season_garden_12_013.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_12_013.text: “Mine would be a mouth with excellent handwriting,” Yue said. Qiu asked whether the handwriting made it easier to obey. Yue considered the private notebook where she tracked what her shoulder could tolerate and admitted that tidy entries sometimes looked more certain than her body felt. She still needed the information. She wanted to learn how to read it without making every line an order. Qiu nodded toward the drawer they had just adjusted. A record could be made easier to use without throwing away what it knew.

season_garden_12_014.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_014.text: Their disagreement returned over the next light sorting task. Qiu proposed dividing the stack by width first; Yue wanted to remove pieces needing repair before sorting. Either could work, but the difference affected how often they would handle the same cloth. They tested a small permitted sample instead of converting the question into a verdict about their temperaments. Qiu's order moved quickly on the sound pieces. Yue's caught two weakened edges before they were folded tightly. They made a combined sequence for this actual stack, with the responsible worker's agreement.

season_garden_12_015.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_015.text: The result pleased Yue until Qiu pointed out that the combined sequence still needed a person to inspect each piece. It had not made attention unnecessary. Yue heard an accusation she had not meant to invite and answered too sharply. Qiu stopped working. The cloth between them lay half folded while the room continued with its own pots and footsteps. Yue felt the old wish to defend what she had said by adding more reasons. Instead she asked Qiu to repeat the actual point before either tried to win against an invented one.

season_garden_12_016.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_12_016.text: “I meant we haven't found a trick that removes the slow part,” Qiu said. “I wasn't saying your idea was slow because you are slow.” Yue heard the distinction and disliked that she had needed it. She apologized for the sharp reply. Qiu did not smooth the moment with a claim that nothing had happened. She said the reply had made her want to stop offering observations. Yue asked whether she could try again with the next cloth. Qiu agreed, and the ordinary task resumed with a little more caution than before.

season_garden_12_017.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_017.text: A small tear near the last cloth's corner gave the argument a practical ending. Yue marked it for the worker responsible for repair, without secretly mending beyond their agreed task. Qiu placed it in the actual repair stack and wrote the reason plainly. The sound pieces remained usable. An entire bundle did not become worthless because one corner failed, and the corner did not become sound because the bundle was mostly good. They counted the finished stack together. The count gave them something true to say that neither person's pride could improve.

season_garden_12_018.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_018.text: The family member responsible for the gathering came through with a modest revised attendance estimate. Some people had accepted, others declined, and two had not answered. Su kept the practical arrangements flexible without treating silence as agreement. The family did not owe everyone a place merely because the helpers wanted to see their preparation used. Yue asked whether the selected first improvement still met the changed estimate. The responsible worker said it did within the accepted arrangement, with the ordinary other option still present. Nothing required a new purchase or an expanded promise.

season_garden_12_019.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_019.text: The child's familiar adult brought a small ordinary question about the gathering: could the child leave before the final conversation if they grew tired? The family said yes. Yue watched the relief on the adult's face and realized how easily a ceremonial ending could become a trap when no one named departure. Qiu asked whether the route from the selected sitting or meal arrangement remained straightforward. The responsible person checked the actual plan. The child did not appear to demonstrate the need; a question had been enough to make it worth considering.

season_garden_12_020.speaker: rival_su_yao
season_garden_12_020.text: “We are arranging an occasion people may use,” Su said after the check. “We are not arranging proof that everyone has understood grief correctly.” Yue had thought the same thing in fragments and was grateful for the plain sentence. Qiu asked whether Su found every such arrangement easier with experience. Su said experience supplied more examples of how people surprised her. It made her more willing to ask, not magically better at knowing answers in advance. She returned to the current paper and crossed out an unnecessary assumption about when everyone would arrive.

season_garden_12_021.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_021.text: The cook offered them a small taste of the ordinary broth she was making for the hall, separate from the later gathering's food. Qiu wanted to identify every flavor and was wrong about one. Yue was wrong about another. The cook laughed and said they could still drink it. The broth reminded Yue of the grandmother's ginger complaint and then of no one in particular; it was warm liquid on an ordinary working day. She drank slowly, allowing the remembered voice and the actual taste to share a moment without forcing one to explain the other.

season_garden_12_022.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_022.text: The last light task involved returning the shallow record board to its approved dry place. Qiu checked the loop, Yue checked the folded corner, and the worker checked the shelf where it belonged. Each could have described the action differently, but the board ended in the correct place. Yue felt a modest tiredness that did not resemble either triumph or failure. Qiu flexed her fingers and chose not to add an unscheduled practice exercise to prove that work had left her strong. They were still at Four pairs, with their own bodies rather than a garden's demand setting private limits.

season_garden_12_023.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_023.text: The twelfth session closed after its full agreed three hours. Su paid each helper three copper for that completed time. With the earlier storm's lost hour still honestly absent, each had now completed and been paid for thirty five hours. Combined labor spending reached seventy copper. No material purchase occurred today; the selected planting's earlier bill still determined the material balance. Yue checked the ordinary coins against the account and put her wages with her own belongings. Payment did not turn the emotional difficulty of the afternoon into a bill the family owed.

season_garden_12_024.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_024.text: They left the hall with the light cover accepted and the cloth stacks honestly sorted. The old tree's restricted ground remained under responsible review. The selected planting remained alive under ordinary care, carrying its own uncertainty forward. The family gathering was nearer, with departure and changing attendance now spoken about rather than guessed. Qiu looked back at the drawer cover and said she wanted to remember the looser edge. Yue said she wanted to remember asking before answering an accusation that had not been made. Neither promised that the lesson would make the next mistake impossible.

season_garden_12_025.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_025.text: At the ordinary path outside the hall, they parted according to their actual plans for the day. Yue did not assume Qiu's free time was available simply because the shared task had gone well. Qiu did not turn their repaired conversation into a declaration about permanent alliance. She asked whether Yue would be ready for the next accepted session if nothing in her present obligations changed. Yue said she expected so and would send the agreed notice if it did. A finite arrangement could hold real interest without swallowing every road beyond it.

season_garden_12_026.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_026.text: Later, Yue opened her own notebook at the unfinished private line from the grandmother's last visit. She did not add the plant's new finding as an answer to the missing voice. She wrote the date of the actual garden session and one ordinary thing she wanted to keep: the owner liking newly visible birds while still missing old shade. The two feelings occupied the page together. Her shoulder needed its familiar rest. She gave it that rest rather than treating a full page as evidence that the rest of her life should hurry too.

season_garden_12_027.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_027.text: The garden continued after the helpers had left. Responsible staff held the actual maintenance and clinical work, with new observations belonging to the people who made them. Yue would learn only what she was entitled to learn at the next visit. In the evening she could hear a bird outside her own window and could not tell whether it resembled the ones above the bench. She did not need to settle the resemblance. She shut the notebook carefully, leaving room for the thirteenth afternoon to be something she had not already written.

season_garden_12_annuals_01.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_01.text: At the selected annual bed, the gardener began with the last actual count rather than a hoped number. Thirteen seedlings had been confirmed at the ninth session. Two more could now be distinguished from the small ordinary growth around them, making fifteen confirmed seedlings today. The gardener showed the identifying features and retained responsibility for the finding. Yue copied the count only after understanding which two were new. The four retained seeds stayed in their proper storage; no further sowing was authorized merely because a larger number would sound better in a story.

season_garden_12_annuals_02.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_02.text: Qiu saw an empty space and nearly called it a missing plant. The gardener reminded her that the original sowing positions and the limited later resowing were recorded separately. Some unsprouted positions remained uncertain, and one could not recover a particular seed's fate by looking from the path. Qiu brought her own earlier drawing into the permitted view and compared it with the actual bed. The blank remained blank. She marked uncertainty as uncertainty, without trying to fill the hole with either optimistic growth or a tidy little death.

season_garden_12_annuals_03.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_12_annuals_03.text: “I wanted the count to mean that we had chosen correctly,” Qiu said. The gardener asked correctly for whom and for what. Qiu pointed toward the hall, then stopped before naming the grandmother as though her death had supplied a final grading of the bed. Yue answered that they had chosen an earlier possible display of yellow within a finite season, knowing it might fail. The gardener nodded toward the seedlings. That purpose still described the decision. It had never promised to make the choice safe from all future regret.

season_garden_12_annuals_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_04.text: A narrow leaf lay against damp soil and looked darker than the upright ones. Yue wanted to lift it. The gardener showed how handling at that point could damage the young plant, then performed the appropriate small check themselves. The leaf was not removed for the helpers to keep or inspect. Qiu moved the light record board to give the gardener clear space. Yue stood back with a useless hand held carefully at her side. Caring enough to want an action did not always mean an action belonged to her.

season_garden_12_annuals_05.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_05.text: The gardener described the approved ordinary watering plan without asking the helpers to become its permanent owners. Actual weather and soil would continue to guide trained adjustments between visits. Yue asked what a visitor could notice without leaning over the bed. The answer was a limited change in visible leaf size and position, not every hidden event under the surface. Qiu drew the approved observation distance on the practical board. The distance seemed annoyingly cautious until she saw how a person turning toward a companion might otherwise step across the edge.

season_garden_12_annuals_06.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_06.text: They checked the simple border marker from the permitted route. One corner had shifted slightly under ordinary use, and staff assigned its proper adjustment to the responsible worker. The helpers could clean the lightweight visible face at the supported table after its safe removal. Yue wiped dirt from the ordinary material, finding an old scratch no one needed to repair. Qiu wanted to align the scratch with the new writing until Yue asked why it mattered. Qiu laughed at herself and left the mark where earlier use had put it.

season_garden_12_annuals_07.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_12_annuals_07.text: “I keep wondering whether she would have liked this stage,” Yue said while they waited for the worker. The question was about the grandmother and the green annuals rather than a future flowering bed. Qiu answered that she had already liked one green update, because she had actually said so. Beyond that, they did not know. Yue found the small certainty kinder than a speech about how pleased the grandmother must be. One actual conversation could remain itself. It did not need to expand into permission for every later thing they wished to do.

season_garden_12_annuals_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_08.text: The child came past with the familiar adult and noticed that the bed still looked mostly green. The adult did not promise yellow for the gathering. The gardener said flowering depended on the plants' development and conditions, and today's useful finding was the actual seedlings. The child asked whether green flowers existed somewhere. The gardener answered the ordinary plant question without turning it into a lesson about mourning. Yue watched the child make a face at the idea of flowers that might be hard to see. The bed remained interesting even while failing to provide the expected color.

season_garden_12_annuals_09.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_09.text: A seedling near the approved edge cast a small shadow on the marker. Qiu measured nothing about it; she simply watched the shadow move when a cloud passed. She had been tempted to photograph the moment in her head as proof of steady progress, then saw how a passing cloud could make the visible size change. Yue asked what she was smiling at. Qiu said she had nearly promoted a shadow into an official finding. The gardener looked amused and asked them to keep the board's writing to the observations actually requested.

season_garden_12_annuals_10.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_10.text: The two new confirmed seedlings did not have to be assigned to the earlier or later sowing merely to make a cleaner account. The gardener could identify their present locations and maintained the planting record with its genuine limits. Yue wrote the actual number and the limited resowing already performed. Qiu checked that the four remaining seeds had not disappeared from the inventory in anyone's excitement. The packet stayed sealed in its proper place. Possibility still existed there, but a reserved seed was not an invisible plant already contributing to the bed.

season_garden_12_annuals_11.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_12_annuals_11.text: “When I was younger, I liked potential because nobody could prove I had wasted it yet,” Qiu said. Yue asked whether the seed packet made her think of that. Qiu nodded. “Then I would hate the actual small thing I had done because it was smaller than everything I could have done.” Yue glanced at the fifteen seedlings. They did not know they were being compared with an imagined perfect bed. The gardener asked for the board, and Qiu handed over the actual completed account instead of continuing the argument with herself.

season_garden_12_annuals_12.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_12.text: The gardener offered a limited future observation suitable for the next accepted session if conditions allowed. The helpers could compare the visible leaves from the route; they would not be responsible for forcing a date of flowering. Yue asked whether the family gathering might use a separate ordinary bowl of flowers supplied by the family if they wished. The answer was yes, under that family's own arrangement, but it would not be credited as flowering from this bed. Qiu looked relieved that the need for beauty did not have to become a false agricultural report.

season_garden_12_annuals_13.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_13.text: A hall visitor asked whether the bed had been planted in the grandmother's memory. Yue explained that it had been selected earlier for a garden used by many people, including an ordinary wish to see yellow flowers. The family had not assigned it a public memorial identity. The visitor accepted the distinction and asked a practical question about the route instead. Qiu helped with the ordinary visible directions permitted to her. The bed did not become less meaningful because its history could not be compressed into the visitor's first guess.

season_garden_12_annuals_14.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_14.text: After the visitor left, Yue felt an impulse to explain more. The grandmother's death had made her afraid that a plain answer would let the woman's presence disappear. Qiu asked which private detail she wanted to make public and who had authorized it. Yue found no answer she liked. She could keep the actual conversations in her own permitted memory without recruiting a stranger to carry them. Qiu did not celebrate the restraint. Both stood for a quiet moment near the living bed and missed a person who would not see the next leaf.

season_garden_12_annuals_15.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_15.text: The selected annual purchase remained three copper, with the earlier bench repair bringing material spending to nine. Thirty one copper of the material allowance remained. The count of confirmed seedlings did not change the supplier's actual price or create a new debt. Su checked the simple arithmetic against the existing record while the gardener kept the plant details. Yue appreciated the separate work. A loss in the family and uncertain germination could make an afternoon emotionally complicated without making the treasury's ordinary subtraction mysterious.

season_garden_12_annuals_16.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_16.text: The gardener found a small ordinary competing plant where it should be removed and performed the trained action. Yue noticed how little ceremony accompanied it. Nothing flashed; no cultivation aura separated desirable growth from unwanted growth by moral judgment. The gardener used knowledge, fingers and attention to the particular bed. Qiu asked why another nearby plant was left. The answer involved its location and present effect, not a universal rule that every green thing in that shape was good or bad. Qiu made a private note to distrust her first elegant explanation.

season_garden_12_annuals_17.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_12_annuals_17.text: “My elegant explanations are usually the ones I give before I bend down far enough to see,” Yue said. Qiu said hers tended to arrive with measurements, which gave them an unfair advantage in arguments. The gardener told both to stop leaning and use the permitted position. They straightened at once, laughed, and returned their attention to the actual board. Yue liked that their growing understanding had not made them immune to a simple reminder. They could learn and still need someone responsible to say where their feet belonged.

season_garden_12_annuals_18.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_18.text: The cleaned lightweight marker was returned by the responsible worker. Its actual placement kept the route distinct from the bed without making the annuals look fenced away from every glance. Yue tested the writing from the permitted standing position. Qiu tested it from the ordinary lower sight line the worker indicated, keeping her body out of the planting area. They found the count legible and the statement modest. Fifteen confirmed seedlings, further development uncertain. The words did not contain a promise about yellow at the gathering, so nobody would need to apologize for a promise they had never made.

season_garden_12_annuals_19.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_19.text: The child had left, and the family member passed alone carrying the ordinary errands of a day after bereavement. She asked for the brief actual plant finding and chose not to take a written copy. Yue told her the confirmed number and the ongoing care. The woman said green was easier to look at today than yellow might have been. She did not explain further. Qiu held the board quietly while the woman continued indoors. The helpers would not revise the planting purpose every time grief changed the way a color felt.

season_garden_12_annuals_20.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_annuals_20.text: Before returning to the hall, Yue looked at the fifteen small plants from the accepted route. The bed held fewer visible lives than the twenty eight seeds actually used, with uncertainty rather than a complete accounting of every absence. It also held more visible lives than it had at the last review. Both findings were true at once. Qiu put the gauge away without using it on a leaf. The actual choice had brought this bed into being, and ordinary care would take it beyond the afternoon without needing the helpers to declare what it meant.

season_garden_12_plum_01.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_01.text: At the selected young plum, the gardener began with the three leaves confirmed during the ninth session. Two more were now visibly opened, making five leaves in the actual limited observation. The little tree still looked sparse beside the established orchard growth. Yue felt a brief unreasonable shame at its smallness, as though the family had paid for grandeur and received a twig. The gardener checked the support and the plant's condition using their own trained judgment. Establishment had always been the purpose. It was not a shortcut to a shaded gathering or fruit this season.

season_garden_12_plum_02.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_02.text: The storm damaged tip had been handled through the gardener's earlier authorized care. Today's check did not pretend the injury had never existed; the appropriate record remained with the people maintaining the tree. Qiu wanted to compare a perfect outline from before the storm with the present shape. Yue asked whether the comparison would answer a useful maintenance question or only make her resent the weather. Qiu set the old sketch aside for a moment. The gardener could use it if needed, but the tree did not have to resemble a drawing to remain worth caring for.

season_garden_12_plum_03.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_12_plum_03.text: “I keep wanting its future to reimburse us for waiting,” Qiu said. Yue looked at the small leaves and asked what payment she had imagined. Qiu named shade, flowers, a moment when someone would say the long choice had been wise. The gardener answered only the plant question: future growth depended on continued care and conditions, and none of those results had been guaranteed here. Qiu breathed out. “I know. I wanted a person to promise it anyway.” The honesty sounded less impressive than confidence and stayed with Yue longer.

season_garden_12_plum_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_04.text: A tie needed the gardener's trained check as the plant and support changed. Yue did not tighten it on intuition. The responsible person showed how an apparently helpful grip could restrict growth, then made the appropriate adjustment themselves. Qiu watched the small space left between material and living surface. Her own gauge could indicate distance but could not decide the tree's care without the gardener's knowledge. She placed it flat on the supported board. Not using a familiar tool was briefly more difficult than finding a measurement to take.

season_garden_12_plum_05.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_05.text: The gardener described how ordinary observation would continue between the helpers' visits. The tree's water and support remained staff responsibilities under the existing maintenance arrangement. Yue asked which change an ordinary visitor could reasonably see without touching it. Five leaves, a modest altered outline, and the fact that the tree was still young. Qiu wrote those things rather than listing invisible roots as though they had personally examined them. The empty ground around the trunk had a purpose. Filling it with decorative objects would not be an innocent way to make the little tree look less alone.

season_garden_12_plum_06.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_06.text: A light removable marker had collected dirt and could be cleaned at the supported table after the responsible worker removed it safely. Yue wiped one side while Qiu held the other edge steady. The ordinary stock bore an old stain that no scrubbing would entirely remove. Qiu wondered whether new writing should avoid it or use a darker line. Yue asked the worker which had been most readable before. They chose the practical answer. A sign about slow growth did not itself need to become a little artwork about the dignity of imperfections.

season_garden_12_plum_07.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_12_plum_07.text: “She might never have seen this become large,” Yue said quietly. She meant the grandmother, and the past tense made the thought unavoidable. Qiu answered that they had known the planting's future extended beyond the grandmother's hoped visit. They had chosen it anyway for a garden used by more than one life. That did not make Yue's sadness an error. Yue set down the damp cloth and said she wished the decision had contained less loss. Qiu said so did she, without promising that the annual choice would have protected them from it.

season_garden_12_plum_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_08.text: The child came past with a familiar adult and asked why the little tree had so much empty space around it. The gardener explained ordinary future room and the present need not to disturb the ground. The child looked toward the old tree's absent crown and asked whether this one would become that big. The gardener would not offer a date or guarantee. It could grow with care, but it was a different tree in its own place. Yue watched the child accept the answer briefly, then demand to know whether birds could sit on the support instead.

season_garden_12_plum_09.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_09.text: The familiar adult said birds made many decisions without asking them. Qiu laughed and pointed out that the support was not an invitation to encourage contact near the young tree. The child's imagined bird was apparently enormous and required a roof. Yue drew a harmless bird on a permitted scrap at the table later, rather than turning the planting support into a play object. The child rejected the drawing because the feet were wrong. Yue offered the pencil for correction. The tree kept its ordinary care while an entirely different creature grew on paper.

season_garden_12_plum_10.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_10.text: Qiu watched the child carry the corrected bird away and returned to the actual plum. She had imagined future birds, fruit and shade until the five leaves seemed inadequate. Now the inadequate little tree looked like a real thing with a future she could neither draw nor possess. The gardener asked her to read the practical marker aloud. She did, keeping the statement to selected planting and continuing establishment care. There was no claim that the tree belonged to the grandmother or that a dead person's wish guaranteed its growth.

season_garden_12_plum_11.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_12_plum_11.text: “I liked long plans because nobody could check them this afternoon,” Qiu said when the child had gone. Yue admitted that she sometimes preferred them for the same reason. A distant success could make today's limitations feel temporary and therefore easier to ignore. The gardener was checking the actual support, not listening for a confession. Qiu looked at the changed tie and said a long plan still had to survive the present afternoon. Yue thought of her shoulder and placed her forearm fully on the supported table before continuing the light cleaning.

season_garden_12_plum_12.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_12.text: The gardener offered a later observation suitable for the next accepted session if conditions allowed. More visible leaves might appear, or current changes might be less welcome; neither result would be determined by the helpers' hope. Yue asked what would happen after the twenty session arrangement ended. The responsible maintenance remained with the orchard under its existing ownership, with any new work needing its own actual acceptance. Qiu felt relief and disappointment together. They were not indispensable, yet the tree could outlast their finite presence without being abandoned by that fact.

season_garden_12_plum_13.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_13.text: A hall visitor asked whether the young plum had replaced the old tree removed earlier. Yue answered that it had been selected for a separate ordinary planting position and did not restore the old tree's years or shade. The restricted former ground was still under responsible review. The visitor looked back and nodded, then asked where the ordinary drinking water stood. Qiu gave the permitted practical direction. The encounter ended without a profound speech, leaving the tree neither celebrated nor diminished by the stranger's first impression.

season_garden_12_plum_14.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_14.text: After the visitor left, Yue wished she had explained why the planting had felt important. Qiu asked who needed that explanation now. The answer was mostly Yue herself. She wanted the choice to be recognized so its uncertain outcome would not seem careless. Qiu said she understood the wish and could not turn it into a stranger's obligation. They stood at the approved route and let the five leaves remain five leaves. The young plum did not need to win a conversation to have a place in the garden.

season_garden_12_plum_15.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_15.text: The selected young plum purchase remained eight copper. With the earlier six copper bench repair, material spending totaled fourteen and twenty six remained from the material allowance. Today's leaves did not change the supplier's bill, and the support adjustment used the existing approved arrangement without a new purchase. Su checked the treasury's simple arithmetic while the gardener retained the plant details. Yue saw how useful it was to let different records carry different facts. The family's grief did not have to be translated into either a financial deficit or an imaginary growth account.

season_garden_12_plum_16.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_16.text: The gardener found a small change in the surface near the tree and checked it with appropriate ordinary knowledge. Yue noticed how little spectacle accompanied the work. No novice qi rushed through the ground to announce that recovery had begun. The gardener examined what they could actually see and acted within trained responsibility. Qiu asked why another apparent change did not need the same action. The answer depended on the particular position and present condition. Her first neat theory had treated two different places as though they were copies.

season_garden_12_plum_17.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_12_plum_17.text: “I wanted the same answer for both,” Yue said. Qiu replied that two different answers felt like a defeat for her notebook. The gardener looked at the notebook and said it might become more useful by containing the difference. Qiu made a face, then wrote a private reminder to ask before collapsing separate observations into one elegant rule. Yue watched her do it and wondered how often their rivalry had involved protecting a beautiful explanation from the untidy people it was supposed to help.

season_garden_12_plum_18.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_18.text: The cleaned lightweight marker was returned by the responsible worker. Its actual position kept people from mistaking the young tree's empty growing space for an unused standing place. Yue read it from the permitted route; Qiu checked the ordinary lower sight line indicated by the worker. The simple writing remained legible without claiming shade or fruit in the current season. Five leaves belonged in the gardener's observation account, rather than painted as a permanent promise on the public marker. A current finding could change, and the sign's job was to remain useful through that change.

season_garden_12_plum_19.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_19.text: The child's familiar adult had gone, and the family member passed alone with an ordinary bag of errands. She asked for the brief actual finding and listened to the count of five leaves. She said she would tell another family member if the conversation felt welcome, but did not take a written copy. Yue did not offer the account as a consolation package she was expected to carry. The woman touched her own bag strap, looked at the tree once, and continued toward the hall. Life after a death included many errands that no garden update could complete.

season_garden_12_plum_20.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_plum_20.text: Before returning indoors, Yue looked at the selected young plum from the approved route. It had more visible leaves than at the last review and still offered no present canopy. Its future could be real without being certain, and its small present could be useful without becoming a disguise for the missing shade. Qiu put the gauge away. They had chosen this establishment within a finite allowance, and qualified ordinary care would continue beyond their afternoon. The tree did not need a verdict about which possible history had been the kinder one.

season_garden_12_growth_gate.speaker: narrator
season_garden_12_growth_gate.text: Today's authorized observation belonged to the planting actually selected and established. The annual bed could offer a new confirmed seedling count with uncertainty about unsprouted positions. The young plum could offer a new visible leaf count and a trained support check. Neither account would be borrowed to make the unchosen history seem present. Yue and Qiu would follow the gardener's corresponding work, with the existing material balance and finite helper agreement preserved. Afterwards, the shared practical tasks would still ask for their ordinary attention.
